stemBlocks.value: Think first: Split the division into its number part and its letter parts and handle each one on its own.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p050-q06 from workbook page 50.

solutionSteps.instruction: Divide the a parts using the index law.

strategyBlocks.value: Divide the coefficients, then subtract the indices of a and of b.

whyThisWorks.value: A fraction of monomials is a product of separate quotients: the numbers divide, and each base divides by subtracting indices. The letter b appears to the first power on both top and bottom, so its quotient is b⁰ = 1 and it vanishes. This is the same cancelling you do with ordinary numerical fractions, applied one base at a time.

commonErrors.misconception: Leaving b in the answer as 3ab.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Leaving b in the answer as 3ab.

commonErrors.misconception: Subtracting instead of dividing the coefficients to get 6a.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Subtracting instead of dividing the coefficients to get 6a.

commonErrors.misconception: Keeping a² because only the coefficients were simplified.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Keeping a² because only the coefficients were simplified.

examTip.value: Check your simplified answer by multiplying it back by the denominator: 3a × 3ab should return 9a²b. That reverse check takes seconds and catches every slip.
